title: LLM Analysis of 150+ years of German Parliamentary Debates on Migration Reveals Shift from Post-War Solidarity to Anti-Solidarity in the Last Decade
abstract: arXiv:2509.07274v4 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Migration has been a core topic in German political debate, from postwar expellee displacement to labor migration and recent refugee movements. Large-scale analysis of such political discourse has traditionally required extensive manual annotation, limiting coverage. Large language models (LLMs) offer a scalable alternative. Using a theory-driven annotation scheme, we examine how well LLMs annotate subtypes of solidarity and anti-solidarity in German parliamentary debates and whether the resulting labels support valid downstream inference. We first evaluate multiple LLMs across model size, prompting strategies, fine-tuning, historical versus contemporary data, and systematic errors. The strongest models, especially GPT-5 and gpt-oss-120B, achieve macro- F1 scores comparable to human agreement, although their systematic errors can bias downstream results. We therefore combine soft-label model outputs with Design-based Supervised Learn

translated_title: LLM分析150多年德国议会关于移民的辩论揭示从战后团结到近十年反团结的转变
translated_abstract: 移民一直是德国政治辩论的核心话题，从战后流离失所者的迁移，到劳动力移民，再到近期的难民潮。传统上，对此类政治话语的大规模分析需要大量的人工标注，限制了覆盖范围。大型语言模型（LLM）提供了一种可扩展的替代方案。我们采用理论驱动的标注方案，考察LLM在德国议会辩论中标注团结与反团结子类型的表现，以及生成的标签是否支持有效的下游推断。我们首先评估了多个LLM，涵盖模型规模、提示策略、微调、历史与当代数据对比以及系统性错误。最强的模型，尤其是GPT-5和gpt-oss-120B，其宏F1分数可与人类一致性相媲美，尽管它们的系统性错误可能使下游结果产生偏差。因此，我们将软标签模型输出与基于设计的有监督学习相结合。
tldr: 本文利用大型语言模型对150多年德国议会移民辩论进行大规模分析，发现最强模型（如GPT-5）的标注性能接近人类水平，并揭示出近十年从战后团结向反团结的显著转变。
en_tdlr: This paper uses large language models to analyze over 150 years of German parliamentary debates on migration, showing that top models (e.g., GPT-5) achieve near-human annotation performance and revealing a notable shift from post-war solidarity to anti-solidarity in the last decade.
